questions.question: Where is the headquarter of Indian Bureau of Mines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The headquarters of the Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) is located in **Nagpur, Maharashtra, India**.
 
• The Indian Bureau of Mines is a government agency under the Ministry of Mines of the Government of India. It was established in 1948, primarily to promote systematic and scientific development of mineral resources in India, as well as to ensure proper utilization and conservation of the nation's mineral wealth.
 
• Nagpur, often referred to as the "Orange City" of India, is a geographically central city and a major trading hub, which makes it a strategic location for the bureau's headquarters.
 
• The city offers connectivity and access to various mining sites across different regions of India.
 
• This central position aids IBM in monitoring, regulation, and enforcement of mining operations efficiently.
 
• The Indian Bureau of Mines has a multifaceted role, including conducting geological surveys, carrying out mineral exploration, and providing technical guidance for the mining sector. It is also involved in the preparation of mineral maps and maintains a repository of mineral resources to facilitate informed decision-making. One of its key functions is regulating and inspecting mines to ensure adherence to safety and environmental standards.
 
• Moreover, IBM is tasked with the responsibility of conducting mineral beneficiation studies and development of mineral processing techniques. It plays a crucial role in advising the central and state governments on all aspects related to mineral wealth and mining legislation. IBM's headquartered location in Nagpur supports its mandate by incorporating research and development initiatives through its various divisions and regional offices.

questions.question: The policy of Permanent Settlement was introduced in India in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1793**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Permanent Settlement, also known as the Zamindari System__, was introduced in Bengal by the East India Company under Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
 
• The system was designed as a legal regime to stabilize property ownership and encourage the landowning Zamindars to improve the agricultural productivity of the lands they governed over.
 
• Its key feature was the fixing of tax obligations in perpetuity.
 
• The taxation rights were given to Zamindars, who were expected to collect these taxes from the peasant communities that resided on the land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Permanent Settlement was first introduced in Bengal and Bihar and later expanded to Varanasi and the south district of Madras.
 
• It eventually spread all over northern India courtesy of a series of regulations promulgated on 1st May 1793.
 
• These regulations persisted until the Charter Act of 1833 came to hold.
 
• The Permanent Settlement marked a significant chapter in the economic and social history of colonial India, shaping the contours of social power and land relations in regions it was introduced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.britannica.com/76/130376-050-CDB90B38/Charles-Cornwallis-1st-Marquess.jpg]

The 36th National Games

__
 
• The 36th National Games is coming to an end after a glorious display of sporting performance and sportsmanship spirit.

• The National Games 2022 was held across six cities, Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot, and Bhavnagar, in Gujarat.

• National Games

• The National Games of India was organized as the Indian Olympic Games in the initial years.
 
• Since the 9th edition of the 1924 Indian Olympic Games in Lahore, these games have been held every two years in major cities of India.

questions.question: According to the article 32 of the Indian Constitution, the Right to constitutional remedies is for the enforcement of _____
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Fundamental Rights​**
 
• The fundamental rights are enshrined in PART III of the constitution from Articles 12 to 35.
 
• The fundamental rights are meant to promote the ideal of Political Democracy.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are guaranteed and protected by the Constitution.
 
• There are 6 Fundamental Rights 
 
 
 

 Fundamental Rights
 Articles
 
 

 Right to equality
 14-18
 
 

 Right to freedom
 19-22
 
 

 Right against exploitation
 23-24
 
 

 Right to freedom of religion
 25-28
 
 

 Cultural and educational rights
 29-30
 
 

 Right to constitutional remedies
 
 
32

 
 
 
 
 
 
• Judiciary(Supreme Court and High Courts) is the guardian of fundamental rights. The Supreme Court(Under Article 32) and the High Courts(Under Article 226) can issue the writs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Directive Principles**

 
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of our State Policy (DPSP).
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy aim to promote the welfare of the people, ensure social and economic justice, and create a just and equitable society.
 
• They provide a framework for the government to strive towards achieving certain socio-economic goals, even though they may not be immediately attainable due to various constraints.
 
• While the Directive Principles themselves are not legally enforceable, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• They guide the formulation of policies and laws by the government and are taken into consideration by the legislature while enacting laws.
 
• Over the years, many judicial decisions and legislative measures have been influenced by the spirit of the Directive Principles.
 
• The balance between fundamental rights and Directive Principles is essential for creating a just and equitable society that respects individual freedoms while striving for the welfare of all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Duties**
 
 
• In the Constitution of India, fundamental duties are mentioned in Article 51A.
 
• There was no list of fundamental duties in the original constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties were added to the Indian constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976 on the recommendation of the Sardar Swarn Singh committee.
 
• the 42nd constitutional amendment added Part IV A and Article 51A to the Indian constitution.
 
• Initially, there were only 10 fundamental duties in the constitution.
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002 added one more fundamental duty to the constitution.
 
• Currently, there are 11 fundamental duties in the Indian constitution.
 
• The idea of fundamental duties was borrowed from the Russian constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties are non-justiciable in nature.

questions.question: The Five Year Plans were formulated, implemented and regulated by a body known as the _____ Commission.

• The Indian Constitution's concept of five-year plans was influenced by the Soviet Union (now Russia), which had successfully implemented five-year plans for economic development.
 
• The Soviet system of economic planning had a particularly strong impact on Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• In order to direct its efforts at economic development after gaining independence, the Indian government created the concept of five-year plans.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was introduced in 1951, and the Planning Commission of India was founded to create and carry out these plans.
 
• The National Development Council (NDC) headed by the Prime Minister with all Chief Minister and cabinet ministers are the final authority to approve the five-year-long policy.
 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formed India's Five-Year Plans.
 
 
 
• In 2014, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced to dissolve the Planning Commission and replace it by a new institution named NITI Aayog.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Wah Festival: A harvest festival where the tribes thank their deities for the bounty and pray for future prosperity.

questions.question: _____ is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts excluding borrowing.
questions.solution:
he correct answer is __**Fiscal deficit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Fiscal deficit**

 
 
• A fiscal deficit occurs when a government's total expenditures exceed the revenue that it generates, excluding money from borrowings. 
 
• Deficit differs from debt, which is an accumulation of yearly deficits. 
 
• A fiscal deficit is regarded by some as a positive economic event. 
 
• The formula for calculating is Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure – Total receipts excluding borrowings. Fiscal deficit acts as an indicator of the total borrowings needed by the government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Revenue deficit: 

 
 
• It is the difference between revenue expenditure and revenue receipts. 
 
• A revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
 
• Such a deficit implies that the government needs to borrow funds to meet recurring expenses which may not provide future returns.
 
• The estimated revenue deficit for 2024-25 is 2% of GDP.​
 
• This is lower than the revised estimates of 2023-24 (2.8%).
 
• Revenue receipts are estimated to increase by 11% in 2024-25, while revenue expenditure is estimated to increase by 3%.
 
• Growth in revenue receipts is driven by corporate tax and income tax, which is estimated to grow by 13% each.
 
 
 
• Primary Deficit: 
 
 
• Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments. This indicates the gap between the government’s expenditure requirements and its receipts, not taking into account the expenditure incurred on interest payments on loans taken during the previous years.
 
• Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit – Interest payments
